title: ile-predict (TATLI framework): A structure-based prediction system for intravenous lipid emulsion amenability in acute poisoning

creators.name: Tatli, Mehmet
creators.affiliation: Department of Emergency Medicine, University of Health Sciences, Van Training and Research Hospital, Van, Türkiye; Department of Neuroscience (PhD Programme), Van Yüzüncü Yıl University, Van, Türkiye

description:
ile-predict is the reference implementation of the TATLI framework (Toxin Amenability To Lipid Infusion), developed in the Van Computational Emergency Toxicology group at Van Yuzuncu Yil University and the University of Health Sciences (Van Training and Research Hospital), Van, Turkiye. It estimates how amenable a toxic agent is to intravenous lipid emulsion (ILE, "lipid rescue") therapy, directly from chemical structure. Physicochemical descriptors are predicted with ADMET-AI, and a logistic model calibrated against a 76-drug literature-consensus responder / non-responder reference set converts effective lipophilicity into a probability of ILE responsiveness (leave-one-out cross-validated ROC-AUC approximately 0.93).

The package ships a mechanistic lipid-sink theory score (logD7.4 gate modulated by volume of distribution), a scored panel of 209 emergency-toxicology agents across 31 classes, a self-contained interactive dashboard, applicability-domain flagging for molecules outside the drug-like range, a command-line interface and a Python API.

Method note: volume of distribution is deliberately excluded from the calibrated model. Adding it raises AUC slightly but flips its coefficient positive, contrary to lipid-sink theory - a collinearity artefact, since lipophilic bases already have high Vd in real drug space.

Research and education prototype. This is not a clinical decision tool and must not be used to guide patient care.
